intent_en: To demonstrate the potential effectiveness of gun licensing systems in reducing firearm-related deaths by contrasting a state that implemented a license with one that repealed it.
previous_intent: To illustrate the potential effectiveness of gun licensing laws by comparing firearm-related death trends in Connecticut after implementation and Missouri after repeal.
narration_support: researchers say this shows that licensing works
chart_support: Two line charts showing firearm-related deaths per 100,000 people; Connecticut shows a decline in homicides and suicides after 1995 (licensing implemented), while Missouri shows a sharp increase after 2007 (licensing repealed)
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states that researchers believe licensing works based on the comparison between Connecticut (implementation) and Missouri (repeal). The charts visually support this by showing a decrease in deaths in Connecticut post-1995 and an increase in Missouri post-2007.
